title: GA/42/2014 of State Of Uttarakhand Vs Ram Singh Rana

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MS. RITU BAHRI
AND
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
18TH APRIL, 2024
GOVERNMENT APPEAL NO. 42 OF 2014
State of Uttarakhand .....Appellant.
Versus
Ram Singh Rana ....Respondent.
Counsel for the Appellant : Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy
 Advocate General assisted by Mr.
 R.K. Joshi, learned Brief Holder.
Counsel for the Respondent : Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned
 counsel.
The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT:(per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Ms. Ritu Bahri)
 The State has come up in appeal against the
judgment and order dated 15.10.2013, passed by Learned
Additional Sessions Judge, Almora, in Sessions Trial No. 2 of
2011, whereby the accused / respondent has been acquitted
from the charges levelled against him under Sections 498-A,
304B and 302 of the Indian Penal Code (I.P.C) in Case Crime
No. 21 of 2010, registered at Police Station Dwarahat, District
Almora.
2. The case of the prosecution in a nutshell is that the
complainant (father of the victim/ deceased) submitted a
complaint on 18.10.2010 that his daughter (victim) was
married to the accused on 25.05.2010. At the time of
marriage, the complainant had given dowry to his daughter

2
according to his status, but the family of the accused
demanded Rs. 5 Lacs as dowry. Somehow the complainant
made the arrangements and gave the money and jewellery.
After the marriage, the in-laws of the victim started
demanding a car and Rs. 2 lacs as dowry. When the
complainant failed to fulfill their demands, they started
harassing the complainant's daughter (victim). In July 2010
when the victim had come to her father's house to celebrate
the festival of Harela, she told him about the demands of her
husband and in-laws and also stated that they can kill her
anytime if their demands are not fulfilled. On 17.10.2010 the
complainant received a phone call that their daughter was ill,
you come here immediately. He again received a call stating
that his daughter had hung herself on a tree. When the
complainant reached the spot, he saw her daughter hanging
on a beam in the cowshed.
3. The accused was charged under sections 302, 498-
A, and 304-B of I.P.C. The accused denied the allegations and
sought trial.
4. To prove its case, the prosecution examined as
many as eight witnesses:-
i. PW.1- Father of the victim.
ii. P.W.2- Mother of the victim.
iii. P.W.3- Uncle of the victim.
iv. P.W.4- Dr. Ram Bihari Verma
v. P.W.5- Himmat Singh Malda

3
vi. P.W.6- C.P. 151 Bal Kishan
vii. P.W.7- Jagdish Pal (Investigating Officer
viii. P.W.8- S.I. Bahadur Singh
5. In the documentary evidence, the following exhibits
were filed:-
i. Exhibit Ka-1 to Ka-5- photographs of the
victim/deceased
ii. Exhibit Ka-6- F.I.R
iii. Exhibit Ka-7 Inquest Report
iv. Exhibit Ka-8- Post Mortem Report
v. Exhibit Ka-9- Chik F.I.R
vi. Exhibit Ka-10- Copy of G.D.
vii. Exhibit Ka-11- Site Plan
viii. Exhibit ka-12- Arrest Memo
ix. Exhibit Ka-13- Information Memo
x. Exhibit Ka-14- Charge-sheet
xi. Exhibit Ka-15- Memo recovery of rope
xii. Exhibit Ka-16 and 17- Copy of G.D.
xiii. Exhibit Ka-18- Application to C.M.0
xiv. Exhibit Ka-19- Copy of G.D
xv. Exhibit Ka-20- Sketch of dead body
xvi. Exhibit Ka-21- Police Form No.13
xvii. Exhibit Ka-22- Sample of seal
xviii. Exhibit Ka-23- Site Plan
6. The statements of the accused were recorded
under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
wherein, the accused stated all facts to be false. He further
stated that on 15.10.2010, he along with the victim and his
sister Bimla had gone to a fair at the local temple, where an
unknown man gave the victim Rs.500. Upon asking about the
same the victim could not give a satisfactory answer and did
not even tell the name of that person. The accused and the
victim got into an argument which continued from the temple

4
to their home. The accused alleged that the victim has illicit
relations with that man and due to the fear of defamation she
took the extreme step of committing suicide.
7. The Father of the Victim (PW.1) in the FIR stated
that at the time of marriage, an amount of Rs.5 lakh was
demanded and a chain which they said to have given later. In
his examination-in-chief, he stated that the barat at the time
of leaving, demanded only Rs. 1 lakh and a chain. However,
in his cross-examination, he stated that he gave dowry out of
his own free will. Such contradictions do not prove the case of
the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
8. The Mother of the Victim (P.W.2) in her chief
examination mentioned that 'Baarat' demanded Rs.5 Lakhs
and Rs.1 Lakhs were given to Ram Singh after borrowing
from a friend. However, in her statement under Section 161
of the Code of Criminal Procedure that the accused persons at
the time of marriage demanded Rs. 1 lakh and a gold chain,
which she agreed in her cross-examination, she also
mentioned therein that the accused before marriage asked for
Rs.5 lakh which she said that she told the police, and if the
police has not mentioned it in their records, then she does
not know reasons thereof. The statement of this witness is
self-contradictory and does not prove the demand for dowry
beyond reasonable doubt.

5
9. Dr. Ram Bihari Verma (P.W.4) who conducted the
post-mortem of the deceased/victim gave the opinion that all
the signs found during the post-mortem of the deceased were
that of suicide. In the post-mortem, no such circumstance
was found that the body was hanged. The deceased has
caused her death by herself. Apart from the ligature mark on
the neck of the deceased, no abrasion or injury marks were
found on the entire body.
10. The Trial Court concluded that the statements of
PW-1, PW-2, and PW-3 nowhere state that the deceased was
subjected to cruelty and harassment for the demand of dowry
soon before her death. The mere demand of dowry before the
marriage is not sufficient to invoke section 304-B, IPC. Such a
demand has to be followed by cruelty or harassment to
attract the provision under Section 304-B.
11. The provision under Section 304-B IPC reads as
follows:
"304-B. Dowry death.- (1) Where the death of a woman
is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise
than under normal circumstances within seven years of her
marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was
subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any
relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any
demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death",
and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have
caused her death.
Explanation- For the purposes of this sub-section, "dowry"
shall have the same meaning as in Section 2 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961.

6
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with
imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven
years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."
This section was inserted by the Dowry Prohibition
(Amendment) Act, 1986 with a view to combat the
increasing menace of dowry deaths. As per the explanation
to the section, the "dowry" for the purposes of this section
shall have the same meaning as in Section 2 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961 which defines "dowry" as follows:
"2. Definition of "dowry"- In this Act, "dowry" means any
property or valuable security given or agreed to be given
either directly or indirectly -
(a) by one party to a marriage to the other party to the
marriage; or
(b) by the parents of either party to a marriage or by any
other person, to either party to the marriage or to any other
person,
at or before or any time after the marriage in connection
with the marriage of the said parties, but does not include
dower or mahr in the case of persons to whom the Muslim
Personal Law (Shariat) applies."
Keeping in view the object, a new Section 113-B was
introduced in the Evidence Act to raise a presumption as to
dowry death. It reads as under:
"113-B. Presumption as to dowry death- When the question
is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a
woman and it is shown that soon before her death such
woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or
harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for
dowry, the court shall presume that such person had caused
the dowry death.
Explanation- For the purpose of this section, "dowry death"
shall have the same meaning as in Section 304-B of the
Penal Code, 1860."
One another provision which is relevant in this context is
Section 498-A IPC which reads as under:
"498-A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman
subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever being the husband or
the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such
woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a
term which may extend to three years and shall also be
liable to fine.
Explanation- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty"
means -
(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to
drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury
or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical)
of the woman; or
(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with
a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet
any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or
is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to
meet such demand."
A careful analysis of Section 304-B shows that this section
has the following essentials:
"(1) The death of a woman should be caused by burns or
bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances;
(2) Such death should have occurred within seven years of
her marriage;

7
(3) She must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment
by her husband or any relative of her husband;
(4) Such cruelty or harassment should be for or in
connection with demand for dowry."
Section 113-B of the Evidence Act lays down that if soon
before the death such woman has been subjected to cruelty
or harassment for or in connection with any demand for
dowry, then the court shall presume that such person has
committed the dowry death. The meaning of "cruelty" for the
purposes of these sections has to be gathered from the
language as found in Section 498-A and as per that section
"cruelty" means "any wilful conduct which is of such a nature
as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause
grave injury or danger to life etc. or harassment to coerce
her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful
demand for any property or valuable security or is on
account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet
such demand". As per the definition of "dowry" any property
or valuable security given or agreed to be given either at or
before or any time after the marriage, comes within the
meaning of "dowry".
12. Having appreciated the evidence on record on the
point of demand of dowry, in our opinion, since the
prosecution has utterly failed in proving the factum of
demand of dowry or cruelty on account of non-fulfillment of
demand of dowry as such, it cannot be said that the offence
under section 498-A or that of 304-B of I.P.C. is proved
against the accused persons. The presumption under section
113-B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, would have arisen
only after the prosecution had proved the factum of demand
of dowry and harassment for non-fulfillment of demand of
dowry. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the Trial Court
has correctly appreciated the evidence on record and has
acquitted the accused.
13. Since the death of the victim took place 500 meters
away from the house of the accused and there is no eye-witness of the said offence. The case is solely based upon

8
circumstantial evidence and the case under circumstantial
evidence requires the following 5 conditions to be fulfilled as
per the judgement of the Supreme Court in the case of
Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra,
(1984) 4 SCC 116:-
(1) the circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt
is to be drawn should be fully established.
(2) the facts so established should be consistent only
with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, that is
to say, they should not be explainable on any other
hypothesis except that the accused is guilty,
(3) the circumstances should be of a conclusive nature
and tendency,
(4) they should exclude every possible hypothesis
except the one to be proved, and
(5) there must be a chain of evidence so complete as
not to leave any reasonable ground for the conclusion
consistent with the innocence of the accused and must
show that in all human probability the act must have
been done by the accused.
14. The case of the prosecution does not stand on the
footing of the above-said conditions and hence the
prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable
doubt.
15. Keeping in mind, the opinion of the Doctor that the
victim had committed suicide, the fact that the accused was
found hanging at a place which was at a distance of 500
meters from the house of the accused, the infirmities in the
statements of the prosecution witness regarding the demand
of dowry, cruelty, and harassment on non-fulfilment of such

9
demands, we are of the opinion that the Trial Court was right
in acquitting the accused.
16. We find no merit in the present Government
Appeal, and the same is, accordingly, dismissed.
17. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
(RITU BAHRI, C.J.)
(ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.)
Dated: 18th April, 2024
NISHANT
